intro: Equipment operators control heavy machines precisely and keep them running, skills that mining, rail and drilling jobs need. The closest of the 25 careers below is surface mining excavating machine operation, with a 93% skill match, while Locomotive Engineers earn a BLS May 2025 median of $81,410, or 36% more.
why_it_works: Running a dozer or excavator means reading the ground, watching gauges and spotting problems before a machine fails. O*NET rates operation and control at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, one of the highest scores for any trade. Mining, rail and drilling equipment use the same control and maintenance skills. Almost all matches need no new schooling. The skills to add are leading crews and installing equipment.
tips: List every machine and attachment you can run, plus hours logged; employers hire on specific equipment.
Underground mining machine operators earn $74,500, which is 24% more, and are an 81% match.
Railroads train locomotive engineers on the job and value years of safe heavy-equipment operation.

faq.q: What jobs can former construction equipment operators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are surface mining excavating operators (93%), continuous mining machine operators (88%) and earth drillers (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Rail-track equipment operators are 83% matched and earn $70,070, which is 17% more than the $59,850 median for operating engineers.

faq.q: Which careers for equipment operators pay more?
faq.a: 13 of the 25 matches pay more than $59,850. Locomotive Engineers earn $81,410 (36% more), mining roof bolters $78,540 (31% more) and underground loading machine operators $74,500 (24% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Mining jobs often include shift and travel work.

faq.q: Do equipment operators need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than operating engineers already have, including 8 of the top 10. In the closest match, 71% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and most training happens on the job.

faq.q: What skills should equipment operators learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing people, installation, operations monitoring and equipment selection. Equipment maintenance already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so leading a crew or learning a new type of machine is usually the next step.
